As of 345 AM EDT Tuesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Heat and humidity persists today across the
south, along with isolated to scattered showers and storms
area-wide. 

Early morning WX analysis indicates a W-NW flow aloft with the
Bermuda high now getting shunted farther south to the Gulf coast
and Bahamas. The latest radar indicates another MCS not too far
off from the one yesterday aftn, currently located across WV and
moving E-SE. The main difference is that this will not be encountering
nearly as favorable of an airmass given the early AM timeframe 
as well as cooler temperatures even compared to the past few 
mornings (upper 60s to lower 70s). Therefore, this feature 
should weaken further through sunrise as it moves east of the 
Appalachians, though a few showers may brush our northern 
counties through mid morning.

With the airmass overturned from yesterday's widespread convection
across VA/MD, today's SVR potential is highly uncertain. Debris
clouds are likely across at least the northern 1/2 of the CWA 
through late morning/early aftn which will limit or at least
delay instability. The CAMs, which generally did poorly
yesterday show varying solutions for this aftn/evening- the 00Z
RRFS is the most aggressive at brining another more organized
line of storms through the CWA from late aftn into the evening, 
while the other models are much less bullish on this scenario. 
The 06Z HRRR has trended closer to the RRFS solution, so at 
least 30-40% PoPs will continue to be maintained for most of the
area. SPC has most of the area in a Marginal SVR risk, 
primarily for damaging wind gusts, as shear is decent for August
(25-30 kt) with a Slight Risk just making it into our far NW. 
The SPC discussion does note the high uncertainty given the 
current MCS and how this might affect aftn conditions. In 
addition, a Marginal ERO is in effect for most of the region 
(with a Slight nudging into the far NW). The sfc winds are a bit
more from the W-SW today, and given this, decided to hoist a 
small Heat Advisory for the interior NE NC zones along the 
Albemarle sound where sfc dew pts should be several degrees 
higher, along with highs into the mid 90s, leading to heat 
indices of 105+ for a few hrs. Elsewhere, highs will generally 
be in the lower 90s (upper 80s/around 90F far N with heat 
indices in the upper 90s to lower 100s). 

show multiple rounds of MCSs developing in the 
WNW/NW flow aloft. However, where they track and when they 
develop will have large implications to the local weather. Most 
CAMs have an overturned airmass moving into the region in the 
wake of today's MCS for Tue. As such, HREF (as well as most 
individual models/CAMs) show dew points in the upper 60s to 
around 70F Tue afternoon (as opposed to the mid 70s from the 
NBM) and lower surface temps. Therefore, have blended in lower 
guidance for dew points but held off (for now) on dropping high 
temps by more than a degree or two due to uncertainty regarding 
whether or not partial clearing can occur during the afternoon. 
This resulted in heat indices remaining below heat advisory 
criteria. As such, no heat headlines will be issued at this 
time. Will note that latest guidance keeps temps even cooler 
than the current forecast. In general, highs in lower 90s are 
the most likely scenario with locally upper 80s or mid 90s 
possible Tue. Additionally, as a result of the overturned 
airmass, widespread cloud cover and mixed dew points could 
result in very little instability Tue afternoon. HREF mean CAPE 
only shows around 500 J/kg for most of the area (which for 
August is very low). As such, confidence in storm development 
(and especially severe potential) for Tue has decreased 
substantially. Nevertheless, SPC has maintained a marginal risk 
(1/5) for severe storms across most of the area with a slight 
risk (level 2/5) across portions of Piedmont. WPC has also 
maintained a marginal ERO across the area for Tue.





KEY MESSAGE 2...An unsettled pattern continues through the remainder 
of the week, trending to a cooler and somewhat drier start to
the weekend. However, uncertainty remains high.

WNW flow aloft continues Wed through the remainder of the week 
as a ridge aloft is expected to continue through late in the 
week as an upper level ridge builds across the central CONUS, 
and eventually shifts E-SE across the deep south. Meanwhile, a 
trough lingers across New England and eastern Canada. Expect an 
active pattern with the daily potential for isolated to 
scattered storms each afternoon/evening. 

SPC has maintained a marginal risk (level 1/5) for severe storms 
across southern portions of the FA Wed. However, confidence 
continues to remain low given uncertainty in aforementioned MCS
timing and impacts. For now, have largely kept NBM PoPs 
(30-35% SW to 15-25% NE) to account for the potential for 
isolated to scattered storms. Beyond Wed, the pattern remains
